entities.summary: Constantine III, King of Abkhazia (c. 894/899–923 CE), was a pivotal figure in the political and territorial consolidation of the Kingdom of Abkhazia, a significant pre-unification Georgian state in the Early Medieval Caucasus. His reign, spanning nearly three decades, marked a period of assertive independence from Byzantine influence and strategic expansion into neighboring Georgian principalities, particularly Kartli, effectively doubling the kingdom's effective domain and setting the stage for the later unified Kingdom of Georgia. He navigated complex geopolitical rivalries involving the Byzantine Empire, the Arab Caliphate, and various Armenian and Georgian feudal lords, solidifying Abkhazia's position as a regional power.
